paras.text: In Pakistan the social movement of women played an important role. The roots of the present women’s movement are in the Pakistan Women’s Action Forum (WAF). This is the name of an informal alliance of women and women’s institutions. This same forum raised its voice on many problems of women, for example creating voice and awareness against oppression of women and the free provision of legal aid and other services to women etc. These very things supported the social movement of women, and after 1981 this movement is effectively active in Pakistan, so that it helps make Pakistan an Islamic, democratic and welfare state in the true sense. Among their important issues are legal rights, violence and political representation etc. Pakistan, because of present world problems, is a victim of extremism, and extremist trends are growing. This problem is against Pakistan’s Islamic, democratic and welfare reputation. In Pakistan, to resist extremist thinking, a social movement named “Khudi” has been started, which consists of young people. This movement is advocating the development of democratic culture and healthy debate and discussion to uproot extremism.

paras.text: In 2007 the lawyers’ movement in Pakistan gained world fame. This was such a public protest movement which started in reaction to the dictatorial decision of General Pervez Musharraf of 9 March 2007. In the light of this dictatorial decision the Chief Justice of Pakistan had been removed from his office because he was refusing to bow before the undemocratic orders and conduct of a dictator. The Pakistan Supreme Court Bar Association interpreted this step of General Musharraf as an attack on the independence of the judiciary. Because of this movement the judges of the superior judiciary were restored, and today in Pakistan the judiciary is completely independent. An independent judiciary alone plays an important role in the establishment of a democratic and welfare system.

In Pakistan the social movement of women played an important role. The roots of the present women’s movement are in the Pakistan Women’s Action Forum (WAF). This is the name of an informal alliance of women and women’s institutions. This same forum raised its voice on many problems of women, for example creating voice and awareness against oppression of women and the free provision of legal aid and other services to women etc. These very things supported the social movement of women, and after 1981 this movement is effectively active in Pakistan, so that it helps make Pakistan an Islamic, democratic and welfare state in the true sense. Among their important issues are legal rights, violence and political representation etc. Pakistan, because of present world problems, is a victim of extremism, and extremist trends are growing. This problem is against Pakistan’s Islamic, democratic and welfare reputation. In Pakistan, to resist extremist thinking, a social movement named “Khudi” has been started, which consists of young people. This movement is advocating the development of democratic culture and healthy debate and discussion to uproot extremism.

In 2007 the lawyers’ movement in Pakistan gained world fame. This was such a public protest movement which started in reaction to the dictatorial decision of General Pervez Musharraf of 9 March 2007. In the light of this dictatorial decision the Chief Justice of Pakistan had been removed from his office because he was refusing to bow before the undemocratic orders and conduct of a dictator. The Pakistan Supreme Court Bar Association interpreted this step of General Musharraf as an attack on the independence of the judiciary. Because of this movement the judges of the superior judiciary were restored, and today in Pakistan the judiciary is completely independent. An independent judiciary alone plays an important role in the establishment of a democratic and welfare system.

The war entering the north-western areas of Pakistan from Afghanistan created a state of chaos and fear in the country. In reaction to this, doctors, lawyers, architects and other educated professionals in Pakistan, to awaken patriotism among Pakistanis, started the “Youth National Flag Movement” on 13 May 2009. … positive role cannot be denied.

Causes of Social Movements

The important reasons or causes of social movements in Pakistan are as follows:

1. Political Causes

The unstable political conditions of Pakistan paved the way for social movements. In Pakistan there has mostly been military dictatorship, and the length of rule worried serious people. When there were restrictions on political activities, social movements filled this gap in the background. The end of democracy too became the cause of the start of social movements. People rose for the restoration and development of democracy and, passing through different paths, adopted the form of movements. These governments trampled democratic values. These governments took such steps as were an open violation of Islam, democracy and welfare thinking. Strong movements started against these rulers. The movement against the dictatorship of Ayub Khan, the Movement for the Restoration of Democracy against General Zia and the lawyers’ movement against General Musharraf etc. started.

Illegal decisions and attacks on the independence of the judiciary also became the cause of strong social movements. General Musharraf, declaring a state of emergency, dismissed the judges of the superior judiciary including the Chief Justice of Pakistan. This was an illegal and unconstitutional decision which challenged the public. Rising above all affiliations, a strong movement was started in the history of Pakistan. Lawyers came into the field. Non-governmental organisations supported them. Journalists too came out. Political parties supported them. In short, people connected with every walk of life came into the field and ran such a successful movement that not only was the judiciary restored and made independent, but the foundations of dictatorship too were shaken. In the beginning and strengthening of social movements the Pakistani and world media played a very key role …
